position_on_ai_or_automated_calls: Explicit AI-agent framework (row 22): (i) inbound calls answered by an AI agent excluded from A2P; (ii) outbound AI calls with explicit consent for service/transactional purposes (appointment confirmations, OTP voice, feedback, support callbacks) stay in service/transactional category and are not escalated to bulk-A2P "solely on account of the use of AI voice technology"; (iii) outbound AI calls without explicit consent stay fully under A2P; (iv) asks TRAI for a dedicated AI-communications framework (AI identification, transparency, AI-assisted vs fully automated boundary). Concedes non-consented AI bulk calls are a legitimate A2P target.
stated_economics: Per-sender/per-campaign A2P pre-declaration "operationally unworkable" for platforms serving "several thousand" MSMEs; proposes platform-level annual declaration. Flat Rs 0.05/min A2P charge without exemption for KYC-verified senders burdens MSMEs. 11.4% of complaints closed on "CDR mismatch" grounds Aug-Nov 2025.
other_relevant_position: Platform safe harbour: primary liability on the sender (PE), not the cloud platform

consultation: TRAI TCCCPR 3rd Amendment notified 18-09-2026, Explanatory Memorandum
position_on_ai_or_automated_calls: Rejected the human-agent carve-out: "technically not feasible" for operators to tell whether a human participates; A2P definition covers autodialling, robo-calls and pre-recorded/artificial voice; every sender must pre-declare A2P use with CLI ranges, recorded on DLT; undeclared A2P found on inspection = UCC; applies to all A2P calls, not only commercial ones
stated_economics: A2P termination charge ceiling Rs 0.05/min (per-minute pulse) "analogous to commercial SMS", explicitly not the Rs 0.50 telcos asked for, to be reviewed; exempt for 140xx/1600xx/1601xx. April 2026: 15,736 of 20,591 UCC disconnections (~75%) were SIP/PRI (A2P) connections
other_relevant_position: Reg 21A proviso: CLIs from 140xx/1600xx/1601xx shall not be flagged "Suspected UCC/spam"; reg 34A: call-management apps may not tag, block or filter designated-series calls; 1600 not extended to non-BFSI (1601 instead); TRAI may classify senders and exempt small BFSI players from mandatory 1600 (they "may be permitted to optionally use 1600 numbers")
